column3: NASB follows the critical text (“in these last days”); “the ages” is rendered “the world.”
NASB follows the critical text without “by Himself” and “our”; it renders “exact expression of the substance” as “exact representation of His nature” and restructures the verse.
The quotation is in capitals. Stray spacing around the quotation marks appears in the NASB text.

NASB reads “HIS KINGDOM”; manuscripts differ between “His” and “Your.” The quotation is in capitals; “to the age of the age” is rendered “FOREVER AND EVER,” and “the scepter of righteousness” is “THE RIGHTEOUS SCEPTER.”
The quotation is in capitals; “wickedness” is rendered “LAWLESSNESS,” and “exultation” is “GLADNESS.”
The quotation is in capitals and reordered.
NASB follows the critical text (“LIKE A GARMENT”); the quotation is in capitals, and “robe” is rendered “MANTLE.”
The quotation is in capitals. The NASB text has the archaic “THINE” beside “YOUR.”
NASB renders “being sent forth for service” as “sent out to render service.”
